shared_elements: low-relief carving on a tan limestone slab
a band of small repeated marks or signs (hatched row in A, sign rows in B)
quadruped or animal-like creatures in profile (A) alongside human-like figures (B)
seated/crouching anthropomorphic figure with bent limbs
justification: Both are shallow-relief carvings on pale stone slabs organised into stacked horizontal registers, with a figural scene set above a narrow band of small repeated marks and figures shown flatly in profile with simplified outlined bodies. The decisive difference is content and composition: A is dominated by boldly modelled animals arranged in rows on a rectangular pillar with heads projecting in the round, whereas B is a rounded-topped stela with a symmetrical pair of seated human figures flanking a table and two ruled lines of script beneath, a scheme absent from A.
